editorial:
Imagine a guy so hated that almost everyone he knows wants him dead. That is exactly who Vilhelm Gerner is. He is a greedy businessman who tricks his partners with fake stock tips, leaving them broke and miserable. One partner even takes his own life because of Gerner's lies. When Gerner finally turns up dead, shot with his own gun, you might think it is a simple case. But here is the wild part: the police find seven different people who all claim they killed him. It creates this tense, mysterious vibe where you are constantly guessing who is telling the truth and who is just lying to look tough.

You will really enjoy the way the police stage a big reconstruction of the crime with all the suspects in one room. It feels like a live puzzle where the pieces keep shifting. The acting is solid for its time, though the pace is a bit slower than today's thrillers. If you like old-school detective stories, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The police use the staged reconstruction to trip up the liars. While many people claimed the kill to satisfy their hatred, only one person's story fits the physical evidence. The detective realizes that the real killer was the one who knew the exact position of the body and the gun. Once the lies are stripped away, the actual murderer is caught, and the law finally brings justice to the man who ruined so many lives.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic whodunnit mysteries and detective work.
